html:
The Amuzgo are an Indigenous people of the Costa Chica on the border of Guerrero and Oaxaca in southern Mexico, around Xochistlahuaca and San Pedro Amuzgos. Their language belongs to the Oto-Manguean family.

Parts of their region paid tribute to the Aztec Triple Alliance in the late 1400s, and after the conquest they were ruled from Spanish towns of the coast. Amuzgo women are known across Mexico for their huipils, long blouses woven on the backstrap loom with fine brocade patterns. Their neighbours include the Me'phaa and the Mixtec.
